versionRule: The subtype name carries the major: v2 when a declared field changes meaning, is removed, or a v1 reader statement would be false of the record. This file's SHA-256 carries the revisions: an added entry with an absence rule, a new reader sentence or a corrected citation stays v1 and moves the digest and the verifier table row's pin (ADR-0038 section 2).
producer: The reference host of this project, civicaitools.org, through the composed harness (ADR-0033, ADR-0037). Every new record of this producer, full-text or hash-only, declares this subtype.

contentProfiles.rule: When both fields are present, metadata.contentProfile is one of the values this row admits. datHere is the A-G envelope (spec section 8.7, its requirements binding on such a record); default is the plain shape, which a hash-only record of this producer carries. The values and their meaning do not change here.
contentProfiles.readers: Spec section 8.1.1 and section 6.2 state the invariant; section 9.2 check #16 reads it.

captureMethods.note: The capture vocabulary is the profile type's (ADR-0011, the G4 decision; spec section 8.6): chat-flow-stream, claude-code-jsonl-readback, claude-code-self-report. This subtype constrains and extends nothing.

classes.shows: A host that shows the sources a run reached derives and shows this statement (SHOULD).
classes.may-show: A host MAY derive and show this statement; its absence from a page says nothing about the record.
classes.never-invents: No host states this from a record of this subtype, because the record does not hold it; its absence renders as not recorded, never as a default.

absenceRule: Every entry below is emitted only when the producer knows its value (ADR-0024; ADR-0033 section C). An absent key states nothing: a host renders it as not recorded, and never as a default, a zero or an empty list (ADR-0033's honest-absence rule).

fields.values: A calendar date, YYYY-MM-DD: the 'today' the composed prompt stated to the model.
fields.absent: Key omitted when the run's root span carried no analysis.asserted_date.
fields.carriedBy: packages/civic-typed-harness/src/__fixtures__/in-loop-golden.json (2026-10-19); the published records of this producer since harness 0.7.0.
fields.sentence: The model was told the date was {assertedDate}.

fields.values: One entry per manifest source in manifest order: { sourceId, alias, reason }, reason one of configured, not-configured, selected, not-selected, reader-off, not-consented (ADR-0033 section E and its 2026-10-18 amendment). A source was offered exactly when its reason is configured or selected.
fields.absent: Key omitted when the run's root span carried no analysis.sources_offered.
fields.carriedBy: in-loop-golden.json (three entries); the three fixture records of the reference host's flows tests (record-2f32d9, record-397939, record-d887c1 at website 567a7c2).
fields.sentence: Supplies the 'Not requested' group of the chooser sentence (see composition.routing) and, per source, why it was not reached: {alias}: {reason as the host's sentence for it}. The host names the source from its own manifest by sourceId; the record never spells the reader-facing name.

fields.values: One entry per source the run composed, in manifest order, with the base of each composed pack (see below), then one for the composing package: { id, version?, guidanceHash?, guidanceOrigin?, reportedName?, reportedVersion? }; guidanceHash is lowercase hex SHA-256 of the guidance text as composed; guidanceOrigin is present exactly when guidanceHash is, one of endpoint, inline, fallback; reportedName and reportedVersion, on a remote server's entry only, are what that server reported itself as (see composition.components.reportedName and composition.components.reportedVersion; ADR-0033 amendment 4). On an all-sources run the composed sources are every offered source. On an in-loop run they are the sources the model loaded, so an offered source the model did not load has no entry unless it is the base of a loaded pack. A pack (an inventory entry whose calls go to a base server with fixed arguments) is one entry of its own, in manifest order like any other entry: id the pack's id, version <version>+<hash12>, the pack's own version and the first twelve hex characters of the hash its inventory entry states (hash), whose coverage is the inventory schema's definition, not this bundle's (ADR-0033 amendment 3). Its base's entry is present whenever the pack's is, because the base's server answers the pack's calls.
fields.absent: Key omitted when the root span carried no analysis.components. A missing version or guidanceHash is unknown or no guidance, respectively; neither is stated as a placeholder.
fields.carriedBy: in-loop-golden.json (socrata 0.9.2 with endpoint guidance; the router 0.5.0); the three website fixture records.
fields.sentence: Composed from: {id} {version} (guidance {guidanceOrigin}, hash {guidanceHash short}); ... ; a pack's entry is named '{the host's name for the pack}, a pack by {author}, using {the host's name for its base}', then its version, guidance and hash as for any entry. The host knows an entry as a pack's from the inventory entry it finds as civic.packId says, or from a call's civic.packId of the same id, and resolves the pack's name and author only from that inventory entry; when it finds none, it names the entry by its id, as any other entry, and names no author. The record never spells either. An entry that states reportedName or reportedVersion may be followed by composition.components.reportedName's words. Until a record carries skillMetadata.skillText (website #694), these entries are the record's only statement of the prompt's pieces, by hash and origin, not by text.

fields.values: The name a remote server reported itself as, verbatim: the serverInfo.name of its MCP initialize result (the older protocol era) or of its server/discover result's _meta['io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo'] (the newer), from this producer's read of that server, which may have been made for an earlier run (ADR-0033 amendment 4). Written only from that read, never from a pin, the manifest or version. On a remote server's entry only: a pack's entry and the composing package's never carry it. Stated after guidanceOrigin, before reportedVersion.
fields.absent: Key omitted when this producer held no report from the server when it wrote the entry, or the server stated no name; and on every record before harness 0.13.0. Absent reads as not recorded: never as the name in the entry's id, and never as a report that matched anything.
fields.carriedBy: reported-keys-golden.json (the base server's entry).
fields.sentence: Beside the entry, a host MAY say 'The server for {name} reported itself as {reportedName} {reportedVersion}.'; with only one of the two keys, 'The server for {name} reported its name as {reportedName}.' or 'The server for {name} reported its version as {reportedVersion}.'; nothing when both are absent. {name} is the host's name for the entry, or its id as written. The words are the server's own statement: nothing in the record checks it against the entry's id, and a host never shows it as the server's identity, which is the id.

fields.values: The version a remote server reported itself as, verbatim: the serverInfo.version of the same read as composition.components.reportedName (ADR-0033 amendment 4). It is the server's own string, not checked against a release or a commit, and never the entry's version, which keeps its meaning. On a remote server's entry only. Stated after reportedName, the entry's last key.
fields.absent: Key omitted when this producer held no report from the server when it wrote the entry, or the server stated no version; and on every record before harness 0.13.0. Absent reads as not recorded, never as the entry's version.
fields.carriedBy: reported-keys-golden.json (the base server's entry).
fields.sentence: Stated in composition.components.reportedName's sentence, beside the name, or alone when the entry states no reportedName.

fields.values: { url, hash, date }, keys in that order: the address the instance serves its flows statement at (absolute http: or https:, no credentials), the statement's version as lowercase hex SHA-256, and its YYYY-MM-DD date. By reference only; never the statement's content (ADR-0033 amendment of 2026-10-18; ADR-0036 section D).
fields.absent: Key omitted when the root span carried no analysis.flows_statement (every record before harness 0.9.0).
fields.carriedBy: in-loop-golden.json; record-d887c1 (website 567a7c2).
fields.sentence: Where this question's data went is described by the flows statement of {date} at {url} (version {hash short}).

fields.values: { method, version }, keys in that order. method one of all-sources, picker, in-loop (ADR-0033 amendment 2); version is the router's version. This producer writes the key on an in-loop run only, with method in-loop; an all-sources run writes no routing key (website src/lib/evidence/trace.ts, IN_LOOP_RUN_RECORD_ATTRIBUTE, and src/lib/mcp/routing-mode.ts at 567a7c2), and nothing emits picker. A record whose considered.rule is reader-picked states method in-loop, since this producer writes composition.considered only on an in-loop run; the reader's picks are told apart by that rule, never by the method picker.
fields.absent: Key omitted when the root span carried no analysis.routing: every all-sources run of this producer, and every record published before in-loop routing reached production (2026-10-27). Absent reads as not recorded, never as all-sources.
fields.carriedBy: in-loop-golden.json (in-loop, router 0.5.0). No public record of the reference host carried it at 2026-10-30 12:35Z (R10-WEB's census: 61 public records, 13 with the composition block, 0 with routing).
fields.sentence: Shown wherever reached sources are shown, read from routing.method, the load spans, sourcesOffered and, when present, considered. in-loop: 'The model chose which sources to load, from those this question could use.', followed, when the record carries composition.considered, by that entry's sentences, then, when the trace holds a search span, by the words of each find_source call (see trace.searchSpan.operationType), then three groups by the host's names for the sources: 'Loaded: {loaded}', a loaded source the host resolves as a pack, as civic.packId says, named '{the host's name for the pack}, a pack by {author}, using {the host's name for its base}'; 'Requested, not loaded: {source} — {its last load's reason}', one line each; 'Not requested: {the sources whose reason is configured, selected or not-consented, with no load}'; an empty group says 'none'. Beside it the host MAY say 'from a source list given by {router component id} {version}'. absent: 'What chose these sources is not recorded.' all-sources, only if a record of this producer ever states that method: 'Every source this question could use was given to the model from the start.'

fields.values: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the run's harness definition { domain, sources, components, chosenBy } in the router's canonical JSON (ADR-0037 section E). The harness states the value as the router computed it and computes nothing.
fields.absent: Key omitted when the root span carried no analysis.definition_hash: every all-sources run, and every record before harness 0.10.0.
fields.carriedBy: in-loop-golden.json. No public record of the reference host carried it at 2026-10-30 12:35Z (the census above).
fields.sentence: May be shown as small print beside the chooser sentence: 'harness definition {definitionHash}'. The definition's contents are never stated from the record: the hash resolves to nothing until the definition is a node type (ADR-0037 section E), so a host states the hash and no more.

fields.values: { inventory: { id, version, hash }, total, listed, rule, ruleVersion }, keys in that order (ADR-0033 amendments 3 and 5). inventory names the source inventory the run was routed against, by reference: id is the inventory's id (civic for the hub's inventory/civic-inventory.json); version is the inventory's own version in build-metadata form <YYYY-MM-DD>.<n>+<hash12>, the twelve characters after the + being the first twelve of hash; hash is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the router's canonical JSON of the parsed inventory file, not of its bytes, the value the file's .sha256 sibling states. A reader resolves a cited inventory at the hub tag civic-inventory/<YYYY-MM-DD>.<n>, the version before the +, and checks the hash there; this bundle names no inventory version or hash, so a new inventory version is not a bundle revision. total is the number of entries in that inventory and listed the number of them the rule listed for the model's first request, integers, listed at most total. On a run that offered the model a search, a search can add sources to the model's list after that request, and listed does not count them. rule names how the listed entries were chosen, an open string to which a later producer may add a value. directory-set is the sources configured on the instance, less any the reader turned off (website src/lib/mcp/routing-mode.ts:92-106 at 473f3a7). reader-picked is the sources the reader picked for this question, less any the instance has not configured or the reader has turned off: the picks travel with the question and can only narrow the run, so listed is the number of picks that were kept (ADR-0033 amendment 5). considered holds that count and names no pick. A pick changes no consent: whether a question was put about a picked source is stated as on any run (see trace.loadSpan.loadAsked). ruleVersion is the rule's version, a non-empty string; directory-set's is 1 and reader-picked's is 1. test-listed-subset, the rule of search-golden.json, is a test rule that no producer writes.
fields.absent: Key omitted when the run's root span carried no analysis.considered: every record before harness 0.12.0, and every record whose producer did not state the inventory it routed against. Absent reads as not recorded: never as every source shown, and never as the hub's current inventory.
fields.carriedBy: packages/civic-typed-harness/src/__fixtures__/considered-golden.json (a test inventory: 3 of 8 entries listed, rule directory-set, version 1); search-golden.json (2 of 8 listed, the test rule test-listed-subset, version 1); picked-golden.json (2 of 8 listed, rule reader-picked, version 1).
fields.sentence: Shown beside the chooser sentence (see composition.routing): first 'The model was shown {listed} of the {total} sources in the source inventory {the host's name for the inventory, or its id as written} (version {version}).', then the rule's words. On a record whose trace holds a search that returned a source (a search span whose outcome is searched and whose hits are not []), the first sentence says 'was first shown' in place of 'was shown': such a search may have added sources after the first list, and listed does not count them. For directory-set, version 1: 'Those were the sources set up on the site that ran this question, less any turned off for it.' For reader-picked, version 1: 'The person who asked this question picked those sources. A picked source was left out if it was turned off, or not set up on the site that ran this question.' The second of these states the rule: the record does not say whether any pick was left out, and a host names no pick from considered. A rule, or a ruleVersion, the host has no words for is named as written: 'They were chosen by a rule recorded as {rule}, version {ruleVersion}, which this site has no words for.'; a host never reads an unknown rule as a known one. Absent: no count is stated, and a host never derives one from sourcesOffered, whose entries are the manifest's, not the inventory's.

fields.values: { rule: { id, version }, cap, search, inventory: { id, version, hash }, hash }, keys in that order, whatever order the root-span attribute wrote them in (ADR-0033 amendment 5): the routing configuration the run was routed under, as its producer stated it. rule names the rule that chose the sources the model was first shown, and its version, each a non-empty string. cap is none, nothing was cut to a cap, or the cap, a positive whole number written in decimal digits with no leading zero. search is none, the run offered the model no search, or { method, version }, the search it offered, each a non-empty string; the one method defined is bm25, version 1, by which a search returns at most ten sources. search states what was offered, never that the model searched: a search that ran is a search span whose outcome is searched (see trace.searchSpan.searchOutcome). inventory names the source inventory the configuration was built over: id and version non-empty strings, hash a lowercase hex SHA-256; the form of its version is not fixed, unlike considered.inventory.version. hash is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the router's canonical JSON of the first four members. The harness recomputes it and refuses a record whose hash is not theirs, so it states those four members and nothing more: it names no router build and no file. The harness does not compare this block with composition.considered; a host reads each from its own keys. As planned for this producer, which had written the key on no record when this revision was written: rule directory-set, version 1, on an in-loop run whose sources no reader picked; rule reader-picked, version 1, with search none, on a run whose sources the reader picked; cap none on both, since no rule of the router cuts the list. test-listed-subset, the rule of search-golden.json, is a test rule that no producer writes.
fields.absent: Key omitted when the run's root span carried no analysis.routing_configuration: every record before harness 0.14.0, and every record whose producer did not state it. No record of the reference host carried it when this revision was written (website f0c1eca has no writer of the attribute). As planned, this producer writes it on in-loop runs only, as it writes composition.considered, so an all-sources run carries none. Absent reads as not recorded: never as cap none, never as search none, and never as rule directory-set.
fields.carriedBy: packages/civic-typed-harness/src/__fixtures__/search-golden.json (rule test-listed-subset 1, cap none, search bm25 1); picked-golden.json (rule reader-picked 1, cap none, search none).
fields.sentence: May be shown as small print beside the chooser sentence (see composition.routing), after composition.considered's sentences when the record carries them, each part read from its own key. The search, for none: 'The model was not offered a search for sources.'; for { method, version }: 'The model was offered a search for sources. The search method is recorded as {method}, version {version}.' Neither says whether a search ran; only a search span whose outcome is searched does (see trace.searchSpan.searchOutcome). The cap, for none: 'The first list of sources had no size limit.'; for a number: 'The first list of sources was limited to {cap}.' The rule, the inventory and the hash, each as written: 'routing rule recorded as {rule.id}, version {rule.version}'; 'built over the source inventory {the host's name for the inventory, or its id as written} (version {inventory.version})'; 'routing configuration {hash}'. A host gives a rule's meaning only in composition.considered's words, from considered.rule, and never from this block. It states the hash and no more: the hash resolves to nothing but the four members beside it. Absent: nothing, or 'not recorded' where the page has a row for it.

fields.values: The tools array as offered to the model, in offered order, verbatim (the router's output: load_source, find_source when the run offered the model a search, and each loaded source's tools), or a BlobRef when large (spec section 8.7.1 requirement 3; ADR-0033 section C). find_source in the array states that a search was offered, not that the model searched: a search that ran is a search span whose outcome is searched (see trace.searchSpan.searchOutcome).
fields.absent: Key omitted when the producer does not know the tools the run offered. Records published before harness 0.7.0 carry the placeholder [] and are not re-labelled. On a record whose metadata.contentProfile is not datHere (this producer's hash-only records carry default), the whole org.civicaitools.environment block is absent, because the harness emits it only for datHere (spec section 8.7.1; harness format/dathere.ts:821-835); that absence states nothing about the tools.
fields.carriedBy: in-loop-golden.json; the three website fixture records.
fields.sentence: Tools offered to the model: {count}, named {names}.

fields.values: { executedAt, environment: { python, libraries }, executionDuration_ms, comparisonCellPresent?, sandboxId? }, the shape spec section 8.7.4 gives the execution extension. Measured at website 567a7c2 (src/lib/notebook-author/phase-d.ts), the reference host writes the block inside the notebook's own metadata at this path, not at the top-level extensions["org.civicaitools.execution"] section 8.7.4 names; a host reads it where the record carries it. The divergence is recorded in ADR-0038 and not resolved by this bundle.
fields.absent: Absent when the notebook was not executed by the publisher's pipeline (a skeleton notebook, provenance absent or skeleton); then the record states nothing about an execution.
fields.carriedBy: The three website fixture records (executed 2026-10-16 and 2026-10-20). Not carried by in-loop-golden.json, whose notebook is a skeleton.
fields.sentence: Executed at {executedAt} on Python {python} with {libraries}, in {executionDuration_ms} ms.

fields.values: The structured two-clause summary the notebook author produced, stamped in the notebook's root metadata when the author step supplied one (website src/lib/notebook-author/synthesize.ts at 567a7c2). The record's top-level summary (spec section 8.1.1, section G) is a separate field and the one a datHere record requires.
fields.absent: Absent when the author step supplied no structured summary; none of the three measured fixture records carries it, and in-loop-golden.json does not. A host reads section G from the top-level summary and states nothing from this block when it is absent.
fields.carriedBy: No measured fixture record carries it. The reference host's answer view reads it when present (src/components/answer-view/buildChatEvidenceView.ts at 567a7c2).
fields.sentence: The structured summary's clauses, as the host's section G rendering, only when present.

fields.values: skeleton or executed (spec section 8.7.4; ADR-0005). Measured at website 567a7c2 (src/lib/notebook-author/synthesize.ts and phase-d.ts), the reference host writes the discriminator inside the notebook's own metadata at this path, not at extensions["org.civicaitools.notebook"].provenance as section 8.7.4 names it; a host reads it where the record carries it. The divergence is recorded in ADR-0038 and not resolved by this bundle.
fields.absent: Absent on a skeleton notebook written by the chat-flow path; section 8.7.4 has a verifier read absence as skeleton, and a host labels the notebook as a skeleton, never as executed.
fields.carriedBy: The three website fixture records (executed). Not carried by in-loop-golden.json (a skeleton).
fields.sentence: executed: 'Executed notebook: the answer was derived from computed data; re-execution is reproducible against the documented runtime and the upstream data as of publish time.' skeleton or absent: 'Skeleton notebook: the answer was authored in chat; the data fetch is reproducible, the answer synthesis is not.' (spec section 8.7.3 item 4 and section 8.7.4's labelling convention, a SHOULD).

fields.values: load_source on a load span: a call the instance's own loop handled through the router's directory, which no source answered (ADR-0033 amendment 2; ADR-0037 section C). Other spans carry the producer's other operation types (query, search, metadata, find_source, ...); find_source marks a search span (see trace.searchSpan.operationType), and search is a source's own search tool.
fields.absent: No load span is present on an all-sources run, where the model is offered no load_source tool, and on every record before in-loop routing. Then the record states that no source was loaded during the run, not that none was reached.
fields.carriedBy: in-loop-golden.json (one load span, loaded).
fields.sentence: Identifies the load spans from which the chooser sentence's 'Loaded' and 'Requested, not loaded' groups are read (see composition.routing): 'the model asked for {alias}'.

fields.values: One of loaded, declined, no-answer, unavailable, not-offered (LOAD_OUTCOMES, format/vocabulary.ts). loaded: the source's guidance and tools were added. declined: the source needed the reader's permission for this run and was not used; the reader answered Not now, or the producer held no pause in which to ask (website src/lib/mcp/routing-mode.ts:301 at 4777b79). no-answer: no decision arrived; the reader did not answer in time, or could not be asked (website src/lib/sources/decision.ts:243-248 at 4777b79). unavailable: the instance could not offer the source for a reason known without contacting it. not-offered: the call named no alias, or its alias named no source in the run's directory when the call was made.
fields.absent: Present on every load span: the harness refuses a load span with no outcome or another value when it builds the graph (LoadSpanError), so a record never states a load without saying how it ended.
fields.carriedBy: in-loop-golden.json (loaded).
fields.sentence: Per load, the reason the chooser sentence gives for a source in its 'Requested, not loaded' group, read from that source's last load: declined 'Not allowed, so it was not used for this question.'; no-answer 'Not used, because the site that ran this question could not ask, or no answer arrived in time.'; unavailable 'Unavailable. The site that ran this question could not load it.' No reason states whether a question was put or answered: a record states whether one was put only in trace.loadSpan.loadAsked, when it carries that attribute, and that entry's words are the only words for it. loaded places the source in the 'Loaded' group; not-offered 'it asked for {alias}, which was not on its list of sources at the time'. The outcome tells 'the model wanted this source and did not get it' from 'the model never asked'.

fields.values: true or false, an OpenTelemetry boolean (boolValue), on a load span: true when the producer put a question to the person running the question about this load's source, on this load or on the earlier load of the same source whose decision this one reuses; false when it put none. A repeat load of a source in the same run states the first load's value, since it reuses that load's decision and puts no new question. A producer that cannot tell whether a question was put omits the attribute. The value is the producer's record of its pause, not a reading of tool.load_outcome: no-answer is written both after a question that got no answer in time and when no question could be put (website src/lib/sources/decision.ts:243-284 and src/lib/mcp/routing-mode.ts:300-313 at 71460c3).
fields.absent: Absent on every load span before harness 0.12.0, and on a load span whose producer did not state it; absent reads as not recorded, never as false. The harness refuses a load span whose tool.load_asked is present and not a boolean when it builds the graph (LoadSpanError), and does not read the attribute on a span that is not a load.
fields.carriedBy: considered-golden.json (two load spans: false, then true).
fields.sentence: Whether the site that ran the question asked the person running it whether to use this load's source, in this run. Only when the value is true MAY a host say, on the source's line in the chooser sentence, 'The site that ran this question asked whether to use {source}.'; only when it is false, 'The site that ran this question did not ask whether to use {source}.'; when it is absent, the host says nothing about a question. {source} is the host's name for the source, or the alias as written when no source has it. The value is read from the same load as the source's reason, its last load. The reasons of trace.loadSpan.loadOutcome are unchanged and state no question either way.

fields.values: find_source on a search span: a call the model made to the search over the source inventory, which the instance's own loop answered itself and which no source saw (ADR-0033 amendment 5). The span's tool.search_outcome says whether the instance ran the search or stopped the call at its limit (see trace.searchSpan.searchOutcome). It is read as a load span is: the graph mints no source agent and no data-response entity for it, dataSources[] has no entry for it, its activity is the platform agent's and states no civic:sourceId, and the calls after it keep their own spans. The harness refuses a search span that carries error: true, mcp.source, mcp.server.id, mcp.alias, mcp.pack_id or tool.upstream_name (SearchSpanError), so a graph never states that a find_source call failed, or that a source, a server or a pack took part in one. The span does not state which sources a search could return, and a host never reads it as a search of the whole inventory. As planned for this producer, a search returns only sources the run's configuration offers and the reader has not turned off. search, another operation type, is a source's own search tool and not this one.
fields.absent: No search span is present on a run that offered the model no search: a run whose routingConfiguration.search is none, a run whose sources the reader picked, an all-sources run, and every record before harness 0.14.0. No record of the reference host held one when this revision was written, since no route of it offers the search. With no search span, the record states that the model asked for no search during the run, so none ran: a call the instance stopped at its limit is a search span too (see trace.searchSpan.searchOutcome). It states nothing about which sources were reached.
fields.carriedBy: packages/civic-typed-harness/src/__fixtures__/search-golden.json (one search span).
fields.sentence: Identifies the search spans, each a find_source call, whose words a host reads by the span's tool.search_outcome (see trace.searchSpan.searchOutcome). A host shows them where reached sources are shown, after composition.considered's sentences, one call at a time in the order of the calls. Only on a call whose outcome is searched, after its sentences from trace.searchSpan.searchQuery and trace.searchSpan.searchHits: 'The site that ran this question did the search itself. It did not send the search to any source.' A host never shows a find_source call as a call to a source, or as a source's answer.

fields.values: One of searched, limit-reached, on a search span (ADR-0033 amendment 5). searched: the instance ran the search the model asked for. limit-reached: the instance had already run two searches in this run, the limit for a run, so it answered the call with its limit text and ran no search. The outcome says whether a search ran, and nothing about what it returned: a search that ran and returned no source is searched, with tool.search_hits [].
fields.absent: Present on every search span: the harness refuses a search span whose tool.search_outcome is absent or is neither value when it builds the graph (SearchSpanError), so a record never states a find_source call without saying whether a search ran.
fields.carriedBy: packages/civic-typed-harness/src/__fixtures__/search-golden.json (one search span, searched). No golden holds a limit-reached span; capture/search-span.test.ts drives one.
fields.sentence: Selects the words of a find_source call. searched: the sentences of trace.searchSpan.searchQuery and trace.searchSpan.searchHits, then trace.searchSpan.operationType's two. limit-reached: 'The model asked for another search, using the words: {query}', the query as written and set off as a quotation, or for an empty query 'The model asked for another search, with no search words.'; then 'The site that ran this question did not run this search. It had already run two searches for this question, which was its limit.' On a limit-reached call a host never says that a search ran, that it returned anything, or that it returned no sources.

fields.values: The query the model sent with a find_source call, verbatim: a string, which may be empty (ADR-0033 amendment 5). Stated on a search span of either outcome; on a span whose outcome is limit-reached it is the query of a search the instance did not run. The model wrote it; it is not the question. The span states what was asked and not who received it: no source saw the call (see trace.searchSpan.operationType), and the record holds no other statement of where the words went.
fields.absent: Present on every search span, of either outcome: the harness refuses a search span whose tool.search_query is absent or is not a string when it builds the graph (SearchSpanError), so a record never states a find_source call without saying what was asked. An empty string is a query, not an absence. The harness does not read the attribute on a span that is not a search span.
fields.carriedBy: search-golden.json (one search span).
fields.sentence: On a call whose outcome is searched, the first sentence of the search: 'The model searched for sources, using the words: {query}', the query as written and set off as a quotation. An empty query: 'The model searched for sources with no search words.' On a call whose outcome is limit-reached the host gives trace.searchSpan.searchOutcome's words, with the same query, and never 'The model searched'. The model wrote the words. A host never shows them as the question, or as the words of the person who asked it.

fields.values: On a search span whose tool.search_outcome is searched: JSON text of an array of non-empty strings, no id twice, the sources the search returned, each by sourceId (the manifest's id, as composition.sourcesOffered[].sourceId names a source), in the search's rank order, best first; [] when the search ran and returned none (ADR-0033 amendment 5). The rank is the search method's and nothing more; the record holds no score. By bm25, version 1, a search returns at most ten sources, so the hits need not be every source that matched. A hit states that the search returned the source: not that the source was then listed for loading, loaded or used. A source that was loaded has a load span, by its alias (see trace.loadSpan.operationType).
fields.absent: Present on every search span whose outcome is searched: the harness refuses such a span whose tool.search_hits is absent, is not text, is not JSON, is not an array, or holds an entry that is not a string, an empty string or the same id twice, when it builds the graph (SearchSpanError). Absent on a search span whose outcome is limit-reached, where no search ran: the harness refuses hits on such a span. So [] always states a search that ran and returned none: never a search that did not run, and never an absence.
fields.carriedBy: search-golden.json (one search span: two hits).
fields.sentence: Only on a call whose outcome is searched, after the search's first sentence: the hits by the host's names for the sources, in the record's order, each id as written when the host has no source of that id: 'The search returned {count} sources. They are listed in the search's order, its best match first: {hits}.'; for one hit, 'The search returned one source: {hit}.'; for [], 'The search returned no sources.' On a record whose routingConfiguration.search is bm25, version 1, a host MAY add 'The search could return at most ten sources.' A host never says the hits were every source that matched, and never says a hit was loaded or used: the chooser sentence's 'Loaded' group, read from the load spans, says which sources were loaded (see composition.routing). A call whose outcome is limit-reached has no hits, and the host gives none of these words for it.

fields.values: true, only when the producer stated that the call failed: it returned no data, whether the source answered with an error or with a reply the producer could not read, did not answer, or was never sent the call; civic:failureKind is the producer's label for it. Never false. Spec section 8.1.8 defines a failed call as one rejected by the source; this producer also marks failed a call the source did not answer and one the producer did not send (civic.failureKind's values say which labels mark one).
fields.absent: Absent when nothing was recorded about how the call ended: the record states nothing, and a reader never reads the absence as success (spec section 8.1.8).
fields.carriedBy: reported-keys-golden.json (one call, labelled base_changed); emitted by the harness since 0.4.0 on the tool-call activity of a span the producer ended with error: true (capture/provenance.ts:622).
fields.sentence: Read with the same activity's civic:failureKind: timeout '{source} did not respond in time, so this call returned no data.'; unavailable '{source} could not be reached or could not answer, so this call returned no data.'; not_configured 'No live data source was configured for this call, so it returned no data.'; not_offered 'This question was not using this data source at the time, so nothing was sent to it.'; unknown 'The request could not be completed, so it returned no data.'; base_changed 'The site that ran this question did not send this call: {source} did not match what {pack} was written for.'; with no civic:failureKind, the words for unknown; a label not among these six, 'This call returned no data. It was recorded as {failureKind}.', the label as written. {source} is the host's name for the activity's civic:sourceId; where a label's words name {source} and the host has no source of that id (this producer writes the id unknown on a call no source took), the host gives the words for unknown. {pack} is the host's name for the pack, found as civic.packId says, or 'the pack recorded as {packId}' when it finds no entry. None of these says that the source refused the call: unknown and unavailable each cover calls a source answered with an error and calls this producer never sent. Nothing when absent.

fields.values: An open producer label beside civic:failed, stated verbatim; the reference producer's six values are timeout, unavailable, not_configured, not_offered, unknown and base_changed. No normative vocabulary. Three mark a call the producer did not send: not_configured, a call no live source was configured for; not_offered, a call to a source the run had not offered or, on an in-loop run, had not yet loaded; base_changed, a pack's call whose base did not match the pack's basePins (see civic.packId). Two mark calls sent and unsent alike, which the label does not tell apart: unknown covers an error the source answered with, a reply the producer could not read, and the refusals the producer makes before sending, such as arguments that do not parse, a portal outside the run's lock, a pack call outside its filter or a bare tool name two sources share; unavailable covers a source the producer could not reach or talk to, as on a network error or an error status from it, and a call to a tool no source has.
fields.absent: Absent unless civic:failed is present: a kind without civic:failed states no failure. A failed call with no kind reads as unknown does.
fields.carriedBy: reported-keys-golden.json (base_changed).
fields.sentence: The words civic.failed's sentence gives for the label, for a failed call with no label and for a label not among the six. A host never switches on the value exhaustively or treats an unknown one as invalid.

fields.path: provenance["@graph"][] (prov:Entity: prompt, skill, output, tool-argument, data-response)["civic:contentHash"]
fields.values: sha256:<hex>, the SHA-256 of the bytes the entity stands for.
fields.absent: Present on every entity the graph mints for content the producer held; absent on an entity whose bytes the producer did not hold.
fields.carriedBy: in-loop-golden.json; the three website fixture records.
fields.sentence: 'Content hash {hex short}'; a reader hashes the content it holds and compares.

fields.values: The MCP server URL the source agent answered from, as the deployment's source registry states it (or, for the skill source, as the skill-fetch span carried it).
fields.absent: Absent on an agent whose address the producer did not state.
fields.carriedBy: in-loop-golden.json; the three website fixture records.
fields.sentence: 'Answered by {source} at {serverUrl host}.', only when at least one activity associated with that agent (prov:wasAssociatedWith) carries no civic:failed; when every one carries civic:failed, the host gives no answered-by sentence for the agent, and civic.failed's words say how each of its calls ended.

fields.values: The stable registry id of the source that answered a call, on the source agent, the tool-call activity and the data-response entity. The activity of a load span or of a search span states none: the instance's own loop answered the call, and no source did. A source id among a search's hits (see civic.searchHits) names a source the search returned, not a source that answered anything.
fields.absent: Absent on a call no source answered (a load or a find_source call) and on a call whose source the span did not name; the graph never defaults a source id (ADR-0024).
fields.carriedBy: in-loop-golden.json; the three website fixture records.
fields.sentence: '{the host's name for sourceId} answered this call.', only on a call that carries no civic:failed; civic.failed's words say how a failed call ended. The host resolves the id against its own manifest; the record never spells the reader-facing name.

fields.values: The public URL of the platform agent that published the record, a typed config input of the deployment.
fields.absent: Present whenever the platform agent is minted; absent only when the deployment states no address.
fields.carriedBy: in-loop-golden.json; the three website fixture records.
fields.sentence: 'Published by {url host}.'

fields.values: The prompt tokens the inference span reported, an integer.
fields.absent: Absent when the span carried no count; never zero-filled.
fields.carriedBy: in-loop-golden.json; the three website fixture records.
fields.sentence: '{n} prompt tokens' for the inference. Nothing when absent.

fields.values: The completion tokens the inference span reported, an integer.
fields.absent: Absent when the span carried no count; never zero-filled.
fields.carriedBy: in-loop-golden.json; the three website fixture records.
fields.sentence: '{n} completion tokens' for the inference. Nothing when absent.

fields.values: The tool the call invoked, verbatim from the span: the name the model called. Under ADR-0032 a source's tool is named <alias>__<upstream name>; a call the instance's own loop answers has a bare name (load_source, find_source).
fields.absent: Absent when the span named no tool; never a placeholder.
fields.carriedBy: in-loop-golden.json; the three website fixture records.
fields.sentence: 'Called {toolName}.'

fields.values: The producer's classification of what the call did (query, search, metadata, load_source, find_source, unknown, ...), an open string stated verbatim.
fields.absent: Absent when the span carried no tool.operation_type.
fields.carriedBy: in-loop-golden.json; the three website fixture records.
fields.sentence: 'A {operationType} call.'

fields.values: The dataset a data response came from, when the span carried one and the source is dataset-keyed.
fields.absent: Absent when the span carried no dataset id (a search, a metadata call, a non-dataset source).
fields.carriedBy: in-loop-golden.json; record-2f32d9 and record-d887c1.
fields.sentence: 'Data from dataset {datasetId}.'

fields.values: The portal host the tool span carried. Never the run's selected portal: a call that addressed no portal yields a response attributed to none.
fields.absent: Absent when the span carried no portal host.
fields.carriedBy: in-loop-golden.json; record-2f32d9 and record-d887c1.
fields.sentence: 'From the portal {portalDomain}.'

fields.values: The canonical dataset URL, minted only when the span carried both the portal host and the dataset id.
fields.absent: Absent when either part is absent; a URL is never minted from a host the span did not state.
fields.carriedBy: in-loop-golden.json; record-2f32d9 and record-d887c1.
fields.sentence: A link to the dataset at {datasetUrl}.

fields.values: null: an explicit placeholder for a Croissant 1.1 metadata URL, named here because the key is inside signed bytes. No record of this producer carries a non-null value.
fields.absent: Absent on a response that is not dataset-keyed.
fields.carriedBy: in-loop-golden.json; record-2f32d9 and record-d887c1 (each null).
fields.sentence: Nothing: a null states no URL, and a host shows no Croissant link from a record of this subtype.

fields.values: The row count the tool response carried, an integer.
fields.absent: Absent when the span reported no row count.
fields.carriedBy: in-loop-golden.json; record-2f32d9 and record-d887c1.
fields.sentence: '{n} rows returned.'

fields.values: The elapsed milliseconds the producer measured for one tool call, on one clock from just before the call until it answered or failed, on every call alike; on a call the producer did not send, the time until its own refusal.
fields.absent: Absent when the span carried no duration.
fields.carriedBy: in-loop-golden.json; the three website fixture records.

fields.values: The server's own tool name, the name the call was sent under on the wire, when the name the model called is an aliased one (ADR-0033 section B; ADR-0032).
fields.absent: Absent when the span carried no tool.upstream_name (a call to an unaliased tool).
fields.carriedBy: in-loop-golden.json; the three website fixture records.
fields.sentence: 'Sent to the server as {upstreamToolName}.'

fields.values: The operator-facing alias of the source that answered the call, the prefix of an aliased tool name.
fields.absent: Absent when the span carried no mcp.alias.
fields.carriedBy: in-loop-golden.json; the three website fixture records.
fields.sentence: The alias by which the chooser sentence names a source: 'it loaded {alias}'.

fields.values: The identity of the server that answered: the router manifest entry's id, which composition.components[].id also carries, so a call joins to its component.
fields.absent: Absent when the span carried no mcp.server.id.
fields.carriedBy: The three website fixture records. Not carried by in-loop-golden.json.
fields.sentence: 'Answered by {serverId}', only on a call that carries no civic:failed, joined to the component of the same id for its version and guidance hash.

fields.values: The id of the pack whose fixed arguments shaped the call: the inventory entry's id, verbatim from the span's mcp.pack_id (ADR-0033 amendment 3). A pack's calls go to its base's server, so the same activity's civic:serverId and civic:sourceId name the base's server and source, and the pack is the composition.components entry of the same id. The key follows civic:serverId. When the pack's inventory entry states basePins, this producer sent the pack's calls only after the base's reported name and version and the argument schemas of the base tools the pin names equalled one of those pins, compared as ADR-0039 (docs/adr/0039-route-identity-conventions.md) states, from its own reads of the base made before the call; on a difference it did not send the call, and recorded it failed, labelled base_changed.
fields.absent: Absent on a call no pack shaped, and on every record before harness 0.12.0; the graph never names a pack the span did not.
fields.carriedBy: considered-golden.json (one call).
fields.sentence: '{the host's name for the pack}, a pack by {author}, using {the host's name for the base}', beside the call. The host resolves the pack's name and author only from the pack's inventory entry: in the inventory composition.considered names, at its tag with its hash checked, by the entry of that id; or, on a record that carries no considered, in the hub's inventory versions, each read at its tag civic-inventory/<version> with its hash checked, or in a copy of them, by the entry of that id whose hash begins with the twelve characters after the + in the version of the pack's composition.components entry (ADR-0039, docs/adr/0039-route-identity-conventions.md). Every fact the host reads from the entry is inside that hash, so any version holding the entry gives the same facts. When it finds no such entry, the host says 'a pack recorded as {packId}, using {the host's name for the base}' and names no author. The record never spells the pack's name or author. When the entry states basePins, beside a call that carries no civic:failed a host MAY say 'The site that ran this question checked {base} before sending this call. {base} reported the name, version and tool inputs that {pack} was written for.', {base} and {pack} being the host's names for the base and the pack.

fields.path: provenance["@graph"][] (prov:Activity, the tool call of a load span, associated with the platform agent)["civic:loadOutcome"]
fields.values: One of loaded, declined, no-answer, unavailable, not-offered, verbatim from the span's tool.load_outcome; the activity's last key but civic:loadAsked, which follows it when the span stated one (ADR-0033 amendments 2 and 3), on no other node.
fields.absent: Absent on every activity that is not a load; a graph never states a load without it.
fields.carriedBy: in-loop-golden.json (loaded).
fields.sentence: The graph's statement of trace.loadSpan.loadOutcome; a host reading the graph rather than the trace derives the same per-load verb from it.

fields.path: provenance["@graph"][] (prov:Activity, the tool call of a load span, associated with the platform agent)["civic:loadAsked"]
fields.values: true or false, verbatim from the span's tool.load_asked; after civic:loadOutcome, the activity's last key, on no other node (ADR-0033 amendment 3).
fields.absent: Absent on every activity that is not a load, and on a load whose span carried no tool.load_asked (every record before harness 0.12.0); absent reads as not recorded, never as false.
fields.carriedBy: considered-golden.json (false, then true).
fields.sentence: The graph's statement of trace.loadSpan.loadAsked; a host reading the graph rather than the trace derives the same words from it, under the same condition.

fields.path: provenance["@graph"][] (prov:Activity, the tool call of a search span, associated with the platform agent)["civic:searchOutcome"]
fields.values: One of searched, limit-reached, verbatim from the span's tool.search_outcome; on the tool-call activity of a search span, which is associated with the platform agent and states no civic:sourceId; on no other node (ADR-0033 amendment 5).
fields.absent: Absent on every activity that is not a search span's; a graph never states a find_source call without it.
fields.carriedBy: search-golden.json (searched); emitted by the harness since 0.14.0 (capture/provenance.ts:681).
fields.sentence: The graph's statement of trace.searchSpan.searchOutcome; a host reading the graph rather than the trace derives the same words from it.

fields.path: provenance["@graph"][] (prov:Activity, the tool call of a search span, associated with the platform agent)["civic:searchQuery"]
fields.values: The query the model sent with a find_source call, verbatim from the span's tool.search_query: a string, which may be empty. Stated on the tool-call activity of a search span, of either outcome; that activity is associated with the platform agent and states no civic:sourceId. On no other node; civic:searchHits follows it when the activity states one (ADR-0033 amendment 5).
fields.absent: Absent on every activity that is not a search span's; a graph never states a find_source call without it.
fields.carriedBy: search-golden.json; emitted by the harness since 0.14.0 (capture/provenance.ts:682).
fields.sentence: The graph's statement of trace.searchSpan.searchQuery; a host reading the graph rather than the trace derives the same words from it, choosing them by the activity's civic:searchOutcome.

fields.path: provenance["@graph"][] (prov:Activity, the tool call of a search span, associated with the platform agent)["civic:searchHits"]
fields.values: A JSON array of non-empty strings, no id twice: the hits' source ids in the order of the span's tool.search_hits, which is the search's rank order, best first; [] is stated when the search ran and returned none. Stated on the tool-call activity of a search span whose outcome is searched, after civic:searchQuery, on no other node (ADR-0033 amendment 5). The order is the order of the record's JSON: the graph's @context declares no @list, so a JSON-LD processor that expands the graph reads the hits as a set. A host reads the order from the record's JSON.
fields.absent: Absent on every activity that is not a search span's, and on the activity of a search span whose outcome is limit-reached, where no search ran. A graph never states a search that ran without it: a search that returned none states [].
fields.carriedBy: search-golden.json (two hits); emitted by the harness since 0.14.0 (capture/provenance.ts:683).
fields.sentence: The graph's statement of trace.searchSpan.searchHits; a host reading the graph rather than the trace derives the same words from it, in the order of the record's JSON.

fields.values: The composed system prompt the model ran under (spec section 8.1.1 admits string | BlobRef; section 8.7.1 requirement 2 requires it non-empty on a datHere record). On a new record of this producer, executed run and comparison run alike, a BlobRef whose content hashes to skillMetadata.systemPromptHash: the final request's system prompt; on an in-loop run whose loads or searches recomposed the prompt, the earlier prompts are not carried as text and each is identified by gen_ai.system_prompt_hash on its llm_inference span. The reference host stores one blob per distinct composed prompt, deduplicated by hash (website src/lib/evidence/prompt-blob.ts at 4777b79); no prose in the signed bytes (website #694 ruled C on 2026-10-30; the reason of website ruling #411 D3). A verifier resolves and hash-checks the BlobRef through spec section 9.2 check #9.
fields.absent: Records published before the website phase that carries it (website #694's fix, planned before this producer declares the subtype): the text was not carried; the hash where present; the composition names the prompt's pieces by guidanceHash and guidanceOrigin (composition.components). Measured 2026-10-30 over the reference host's 61 public records: the 17 executed-run records published since September carry neither text nor hash; 33 older records carry text and hash; one comparison record carries the hash only. Since that phase, a new record carries systemPromptHash with no skillText when the run-end write of the text failed, or when at publish the stored text could not be read or did not hash to systemPromptHash (website src/lib/evidence/prompt-blob.ts at 4777b79). A datHere record without the text is reported by spec section 9.2 check #17 as skillText_absent, attention and never a failure; every published record keeps its verdicts.
fields.carriedBy: The 33 older public records of the reference host (text and hash). No executed-run record and no fixture of this producer carries it at 2026-10-30; the harness fixture legacy-blobref-trace-skill-override (reference-golden.json) carries a BlobRef skillText from an override and is not a record of this host.
fields.sentence: Text present inline: 'The text of the system prompt the model was given, as the signed record includes it.' Text present as a BlobRef: 'The text of the system prompt the model was given, kept outside the signed record. It is shown only if it matches the hash this record states.', and the host shows the text only when its bytes hash to the reference. Absent: 'This record does not include the text of the system prompt (the instructions the model was given before the question).' when systemPromptHash is present, and 'This record does not include the text of the system prompt (the instructions the model was given before the question), or a hash of it.' when it is not, with the composition's components listed by id, version and guidance hash in either case. When the trace's llm_inference spans state more than one distinct gen_ai.system_prompt_hash: 'The model was given {count} system prompts during this question. This section describes the last one.', {count} including the last. A host never shows a prompt it reconstructs from the components as if the record carried it.

fields.values: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the composed system prompt as a whole (ADR-0033 section E: components[].guidanceHash is each piece's; this is the whole's). The trace of every measured record carries gen_ai.system_prompt_hash on an llm_inference span; the executed_notebook span's analysis.prompt_hash is the notebook author's prompt, a different hash in every measured record.
fields.absent: On every new record of this producer the hash is carried inline beside the skillText BlobRef when the text was stored (see skillMetadata.skillText's absence rule), as website #694 ruled C on 2026-10-30. Before that phase: the 17 executed-run records published since September carry no hash (skillMetadata is {}, while the trace's llm_inference span carries gen_ai.system_prompt_hash); the 33 older records and the one comparison record carry it. A host MAY show the trace's hash as the trace's, never as skillMetadata's.
fields.carriedBy: The 33 older public records and the one comparison record of the reference host. Not carried by the executed-run records at 2026-10-30 (the hash is in each one's trace only: record-2f32d9, record-397939, record-d887c1 at website 567a7c2).
fields.sentence: Present: 'System prompt hash {systemPromptHash short}' in the Model + environment card; with skillText absent, the hash-only state of skillMetadata.skillText's sentence. Absent: nothing, or 'not recorded' where the card has a row for it.

neverCarried.fact: Who consented to a source (the reader's identity).
neverCarried.rule: Never enters a record of this subtype and no host states it from one. The consent itself is kept in the app's own store (the MCP-sources design, sections 1.6 and 4.4; ADR-0036). A record states only that a load was asked for, how it ended, and, where it carries trace.loadSpan.loadAsked, whether a question was put; never who answered it.

neverCarried.fact: When consent was given or withdrawn.
neverCarried.rule: Never enters a record; no host states a consent time from one. The load span's own timing is the call's, not the consent's.

neverCarried.fact: The reader's account (the consent row's account column).
neverCarried.rule: Never enters a record. A record's signer is the platform or the publisher, never the consenting reader.

neverCarried.fact: The reader's per-source consent states (On, Ask first, Off) as stored.
neverCarried.rule: Never enters a record as a field. sourcesOffered[].reason states the state's effect on the run (reader-off, not-consented), which is an outcome for one run and not the stored state. A record's notebook text, written at run time, may name the setting the site applied (the reference host's notebook says a declined source was 'not used, set to Ask first', website src/lib/notebook-author/tool-to-cell.ts:1169 at 4777b79); no host derives a consent state from that text or from any other part of a record, and a host never reconstructs the consent panel from a record.

neverCarried.fact: The flows-version row of the consent store (which statement version the reader consented under).
neverCarried.rule: Never enters a record. flowsStatement names the statement in force for the run by url, hash and date; it does not say the reader consented under it.

neverCarried.fact: The anonymous reader's session cookie or any session identifier.
neverCarried.rule: Never enters a record; no host states one from a record.

neverCarried.fact: The flows statement's text (the recipients, what each receives, the postures their holders state).
neverCarried.rule: Never enters a record: the harness refuses a flowsStatement with any key beyond url, hash and date (format/dathere.ts). A host that shows the statement fetches it by url and checks the hash; it never presents the text as if the record carried it.
